methodology_note: Every grading-model and verified-scorer fact in review.md and scorers/verified.md holds in the v1.0.1 snapshot and the working-repo scorer. I rebuilt each task in the snapshot (no_knowledge retrieval variant, same toolkit and DB, gold-derived read_log_allowlist), replayed gold and the alternatives the review cites, and compared with a verbatim copy of _verified_db_match/_input_rejected_discoverable_tools. Every divergence claim reproduced, and all 19 gold trajectories replay without tool errors. I also recomputed rewards for all six dispute users under floor and half-up, and both conventions gave exactly the counts the review reports. The review's reasoning is sound and its citations are accurate apart from two transaction-count slips (018: 49 vs 47 rows; 020: 25 vs 26) and an imprecise 'differ only in auto_resolve' phrasing (026). Its blind spot is that it repeatedly uses 'earlier Opus trials' pass/fail counts (014, 015) as supporting evidence that nothing in the snapshot or the run inputs lets a verifier check. Those counts should be treated as anecdote, not proof. The unflagged sample (002, 004, 008) held up under a from-scratch audit.
